sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Strategic Objective**: The Marathas aimed to establish 'Hindupad Padshahi' and secure the **Chauth** and **Sardeshmukhi** rights across Northern India.
• **The 1752 Treaty**: A landmark agreement between the Mughal Emperor Ahmad Shah and the Marathas, where the latter promised to protect the Mughal throne from internal and external threats in exchange for the **Chauth** of Punjab, Sindh, and the Doab.
• **Geopolitical Vacuum**: The collapse of the Mughal central authority post-Nadir Shah's invasion (1739) allowed the Marathas to act as the 'de facto' protectors of Delhi.
• **Key Metric**: The expansion was driven by the need for revenue to sustain the massive Maratha military machine, shifting from 'plunder' to 'administrative control'.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Administrative Integration**: Attempting to replace local Mughal governors with Maratha 'Subahdars'.
• **Diplomatic Maneuvering**: Aligning with the Mughal Wazir (Safdar Jang) to counter the Rohilla-Afghan threat.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Logistical overstretch, lack of local support in Punjab, and the alienation of Rajput/Jat allies.
• **Solutions**: Need for a consolidated administrative structure rather than mere military occupation.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'R-A-P' (Raghunath, Abdali, Punjab).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Raghunath Rao's entry into Punjab triggered the direct conflict with Abdali.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 1752 Treaty with the 1761 Panipat outcome. The 1752 treaty was a diplomatic success for Marathas, not a military defeat.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Imperial Overstretch' to describe the Maratha failure to consolidate Punjab, which led to the disaster at Panipat.

keyTakeaways: The Maratha advance was a transition from a regional power to an imperial force.
The 1752 Treaty made the Marathas the 'de facto' protectors of the Mughal throne.
The occupation of Lahore in 1758 was the peak of the first phase, directly provoking Abdali.
